done_when: A follow-up that names a period answers for that period whatever window the model emits; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: The period-word heuristic treats the common modal verb “May” as a month. For example, `May I see Actual by GL code?` has no requested period and `parseTimeWindow` returns null, but this regex makes `hasTimePeriodWords` return true. Consequently the new branch does not clear a model-emitted window such as `last: 31`, so a fresh question does not aggregate all loaded data and a follow-up does not inherit its prior window. This violates the explicit no-period requirement.
findings.title: Not done: A follow-up that names a period answers for that period whatever window the model emits; a question naming no period still

findings.body: The added regression coverage calls `ChatService.ask` directly with a fake LLM and fake executor. It therefore does not prove the required user-facing flow through the running API, real database, and browser: carrying prior turns, overriding a wrong model window, inheriting/aggregating when no period is named, and changing the answer period. The repository evidence contains no Playwright scenario for these behaviors, so the change is proven only at a mocked unit boundary.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
